description:
FILED s473t6a (Opus, 2026-09-16) by #1501 ROUND 8 (t6a), CHECK 1 of
t/op/filetest.t.  PRE-EXISTING.  A PPI LEXER bug, logged as
docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md section 31 + five rows in docs/ppi-bug-report.t
(plan 73 -> 78) in the same commit that files this.

`_` is an ordinary subroutine name in perl; it keeps its magic meaning (the
stat buffer) only in filetest operand position.  t/op/filetest.t lines 159-162
are the test that pins exactly that:

    -f 'TEST';
    is(-f _, 1, "_ is bareword after filetest operator");
    sub _ { "this is not a file name" }
    is(-f _, 1, "_ is bareword after filetest operator");

PPI 1.291 classifies `_` as `PPI::Token::Magic` WHEREVER it appears, including
directly after the keyword `sub`.  PPI::Lexer's Statement::Sub rule needs a
`Token::Word` there, so it does not fire and the whole thing becomes ONE plain
`PPI::Statement` that runs on past the block and SWALLOWS the next statement:

  $ perl -MPPI -e 'my $d = PPI::Document->new(\q{sub _ { "x" } print 1;});
                   for my $e ($d->schildren) { print ref($e), ": ", $e->content, "\n" }'
  PPI::Statement: sub _ { "x" } print 1;

PCL then DROPS it (`Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ['Token::Magic<_>', ...]`)
and the die that follows (`Undefined subroutine &main::f called`) aborts the
top-level form.  Measured (scratch/s473t6a/probes/ft-underscore.pl): perl
prints 1 and 1; PCL prints the first and loses the rest.

ROWS: t/op/filetest.t's two `_ is bareword after filetest operator` rows, which
the SHORTFALL bucket sees (2 rows never produced) plus the file's `*summary*`
renumber.  The whole-file cost is small; the LEXER bug is not, because a sub
named `_` is legal and swallows its neighbour wherever it appears.

FIX SHAPE: a `_ppi_parse` in-place token repair in the family PCL already has
(`_reclassify_bare_vwords`, `_merge_unicode_symbols`,
`_merge_punct_array_symbols`, `_repair_indented_heredocs`): a `Token::Magic`
whose content is `_` and whose previous significant sibling is the Word `sub`
is re-classed as a `Token::Word`, and the document re-lexed.  The forward
declaration `sub _;` needs the same.  PROBE THE BREAKING CASE: `-f _` must
KEEP reading the stat buffer after the repair (that is what the test asserts),
and `sub main::_ { }` already lexes correctly, so the repair must not touch it.
subject: PPI 1.291 lexes the NAME `_` after `sub` as Token::Magic, so `sub _ { }` builds no Statement::Sub and SWALLOWS the next statement (ppi-upstream-bugs.md 31)
